paper.title: The effect of integration policies on the time until regular employment of newly arrived immigrants: Evidence from Denmark
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement. The paper states only: 'We use data from several administrative registers, which are collected and merged by Statistics Denmark.' (p. 412). No DST project reference is given.

registers.name_in_paper: several administrative registers, collected and merged by Statistics Denmark
registers.years: 2000-2002 (residence-permit cohorts; weekly event histories from the date of residence permit to the last week of the sample period)
registers.role: sample frame, treatment (ALMP and language-course participation), outcome (transition to regular employment), controls

linkages: Weekly event histories for labour-market states, including Danish language course participation, ALMP participation and employment, constructed for each immigrant from the merged administrative registers
Demographic and socio-economic variables (children, marital status and spouse's immigrant status, country of origin, basis for residence permit, doctor visits, housing) linked to the individual
Local labour-market conditions and immigrant concentration linked through the municipality of residence

sample.universe: All immigrants in Denmark who (1) received their residence permit in 2000-2002, (2) were 16-64 years of age at the time of arrival, (3) are from non-EU and non-Nordic countries, and (4) are refugees or family reunified
sample.unit_of_observation: immigrant (individual duration spell from the date of residence permit, with weekly event history; durations measured in weeks)
selection_rules: Residence permit received in 2000-2002 (ALMP participation data are not available before 2000; 2002 is the last observation year in the dataset)
16-64 years of age at the time of arrival
Sub-sample: received social assistance from the time of the residence permit
Event histories end in the last week of the sample period or, in case of emigration or death, at the date of this event
Spells of persons participating in more than one programme are right censored at the duration where the second programme period begins
sample.period: Residence permits 2000-2002; weekly event histories from the date of residence permit
sample.n_individuals: 21,568 immigrants; of these 13,734 received social assistance from the time of residence permit and 7,834 did not

construction_notes: Durations are measured in weeks from the date of residence permit; the piecewise constant baseline hazards use quarterly intervals (hm = 13m since the time unit is weeks), with nine duration-dependent constant terms that are not reported.

Initial proficiency in Danish (initial) is constructed from the track, level and sublevel at which the immigrant starts language courses (Fig. 1) and takes values between -2 and 3 2/3 in steps of 1/3.

Progression in proficiency is measured in deviations from the initial level and is observed when an immigrant begins taking courses at a higher level or sublevel; completion of courses is not observed. Initial proficiency plus progression gives current proficiency.

For immigrants who neither participate nor have participated in language courses, the initial-proficiency and progression variables are set to zero (no information on proficiency is available for them).
The reported coefficient of participating in language courses on track 1 has two times the coefficient of initial proficiency in Danish subtracted (note to Table 2).
Two linear restrictions are imposed in Model 3: the difference between the coefficients of 'Participates on track j of language courses' and 'Has participated on track j' are equal for j = 1,2,3.
Only the first ALMP spell per person is used; about 20% of ALMP participants participate more than once and those spells are right censored at the start of the second programme period.
'Age' and 'number of visits to the doctor' are categorised to allow for non-linear effects; alternative categorisations did not change the main results.

Marginal effects (Table 3) are differences in restricted mean durations up to Tmax = 4 years, measured in weeks, computed for a 'reference person' (female, single, no children, 35-44 years of age, from Iraq, family reunified to a non-refugee, not living in a socially deprived neighbourhood) and average municipal characteristics, averaged over 55 programme spells and 82 language-course spells (4510 combinations).
Standard errors of the marginal effects are the standard deviations of 500 marginal effects calculated from random draws of the estimated parameter vector.

links.pointer_quote: We find significant and substantial lock-in effects of participation in labour-market programmes on the hazard rate to regular employment.

claims.statement: While participating in an active labour-market programme, the hazard rate to regular employment of all immigrants is reduced (lock-in effect), with programme types pooled.

treatment.label: Participates in a labour-market programme (lock-in effect)

definition.value: Time-varying indicator d1(t) equal to 1 while the immigrant is participating in an active labour-market programme at elapsed duration t, and 0 otherwise; Model 1 does not distinguish between the six programme types. Only the first ALMP spell is used.

timing.value: Contemporaneous: measured week by week since the date of residence permit, while the programme is ongoing.

definition.value: The exit rate from the date of residence permit into regular employment, modelled as a mixed proportional hazard (equation (4)) on weekly event histories; the reported coefficient is the change in the logarithm of this hazard rate per one-unit change in the variable.

timing.value: Weekly event history beginning at the date of residence permit and ending in the last week of the sample period (or at emigration or death); durations are measured in weeks and the baseline hazard is piecewise constant over quarters.

units.value: change in the logarithm of the hazard rate to regular employment when the variable is changed by one unit, holding all other variables constant (log hazard ratio)

magnitude.interpretation: In model 1 the lock-in effects of these programmes on the hazard rate to employment are described as large (numerically) and significant.

estimand.target_population: Newly arrived immigrants in Denmark covered by the municipal integration programme: immigrants who (1) received their residence permit in 2000-2002, (2) were 16-64 years of age at the time of arrival, (3) are from non-EU and non-Nordic countries, (4) are refugees or family reunified.
estimand.time_horizon: During participation in the programme (contemporaneous effect on the weekly hazard rate while the programme is ongoing)

population.description: All immigrants who (1) received their residence permit in 2000-2002, (2) were 16-64 years of age at the time of arrival, (3) are from non-EU and non-Nordic countries, (4) are refugees or family reunified (21,568 immigrants).

Immigrants who received social assistance from the time of residence permit
Language-course participants, by track (1, 2, 3)
Participants in each of the six types of active labour-market programme
population.selection: Administrative universe of immigrants in Denmark, restricted to those receiving a residence permit in 2000-2002 (ALMP participation data are not available before 2000; 2002 is the last observation year), aged 16-64 at arrival, from non-EU and non-Nordic countries, and refugees or family reunified.

identification.source_of_variation: Variation in the timing of entry into active labour-market programmes among newly arrived immigrants: the duration from residence permit to programme entry is modelled jointly with the duration to regular employment (timing-of-events model of Abbring and van den Berg, 2003), and selection on unobservables is captured by correlated, time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity. No instrument and no exclusion restriction is used.

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: a treatment starting at time t does not affect the outcome state (employment or non-employment) before time t.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Argued, not tested: the authors say immigrants typically cannot predict either the time of treatment or the specific programme to which they may be assigned. Given this assumption, no exclusion restrictions are needed.

implies_edges.from: Entry into an active labour-market programme at time t
implies_edges.to: Hazard rate to regular employment before time t

key_assumptions.assumption: Mixed proportional hazard (MPH) specification of both the employment hazard and the programme-entry hazards, with piecewise constant baseline hazards.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as the modelling assumption under which the treatment effects are non-parametrically identified; not tested.

formal.as_written: θu(tu|x(tu), d1(tu), d2(tu), νu) = λu(tu) exp(x(tu)βu + d1(tu)δ1 + d2(tu)δ2 + νu)

key_assumptions.assumption: Selection into programmes on unobservables is captured by time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity terms that are allowed to be correlated across the employment hazard and the programme hazards.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Built into the likelihood: the correlation between the unobserved term in the employment hazard and those in the programme hazards is unrestricted; no separate test is reported.

key_assumptions.assumption: The joint distribution of the unobserved heterogeneity terms is discrete with 2 x 2 mass points (Heckman and Singer), so the unobserved components of selection into the J programmes are perfectly correlated.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as a simplification; the paper notes that the number of mass points found in applications of this method is typically low.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimated effects are effects of the first ALMP spell: spells of persons participating more than once are right censored at the duration where the second programme period begins.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated in the data section; about 20% of ALMP participants participate more than once.

threats_discussed: Non-random selection into labour-market programmes on observed and unobserved covariates
Endogeneity of the decision to participate in language training and of progression in language proficiency (selection into language courses is not modelled)
No information on proficiency in Danish for immigrants who have not participated in language courses (31% of all immigrants, 24% of those initially receiving social assistance)
Short observation period, so the estimates are short-run estimates in which the negative lock-in effects are relatively important
robustness_checks: Three model specifications (Model 1: ALMPs pooled; Model 2: six programme types; Model 3: adds language-course track placement and lock-in interaction effects), each estimated on two samples
Alternative categorisations of 'age' and 'number of visits to the doctor' did not change the main results
Post-programme interaction effects for simultaneous participation in language courses and ALMPs were estimated and were clearly insignificant
unresolved_confounders: No information on labour-market experience in the country of origin
No information on educational level, except that track placement for language-course participants indicates whether the person is illiterate or has a low or high level of schooling
No information on proficiency in Danish for immigrants who have not participated in language courses

definition.value: Time-varying indicator d1j(t) equal to 1 while the immigrant is participating in counselling and upgrading programmes, primarily introduction programmes and counselling regarding employment and education options, and 0 otherwise; at most one programme indicator is equal to 1 at a given time. Only the first ALMP spell is used.

timing.value: Contemporaneous: week by week since the date of residence permit, while the programme is ongoing.

definition.value: The exit rate from the date of residence permit into regular employment, modelled as a mixed proportional hazard (equation (4)) on weekly event histories; the reported coefficient is the change in the logarithm of this hazard rate per one-unit change in the variable.

timing.value: Weekly event history beginning at the date of residence permit and ending in the last week of the sample period (or at emigration or death); durations are measured in weeks and the baseline hazard is piecewise constant over quarters.

units.value: change in the logarithm of the hazard rate to regular employment when the variable is changed by one unit, holding all other variables constant (log hazard ratio)

estimand.target_population: Newly arrived immigrants covered by the municipal integration programme who received social assistance from the time of residence permit (the group to which ALMPs are primarily offered).
estimand.time_horizon: During participation in the programme (contemporaneous effect on the weekly hazard rate while the programme is ongoing)

population.description: The sub-sample of immigrants who (1) received their residence permit in 2000-2002, (2) were 16-64 years of age at the time of arrival, (3) are from non-EU and non-Nordic countries, (4) are refugees or family reunified who received social assistance from the time when they got their residence permit (13,734 immigrants).
population.ages: 16-64 years of age at the time of arrival / at receipt of the residence permit
population.period: Residence permits granted in 2000-2002; event histories followed from the date of residence permit
subgroups_defined: All immigrants meeting the four criteria
Immigrants who received social assistance from the time of residence permit
Language-course participants, by track (1, 2, 3)
Participants in each of the six types of active labour-market programme
population.selection: As for all immigrants, further conditioned on receiving social assistance from the time of the residence permit.

identification.source_of_variation: Variation in the timing of entry into active labour-market programmes among newly arrived immigrants: the duration from residence permit to programme entry is modelled jointly with the duration to regular employment (timing-of-events model of Abbring and van den Berg, 2003), and selection on unobservables is captured by correlated, time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity. No instrument and no exclusion restriction is used.

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: a treatment starting at time t does not affect the outcome state (employment or non-employment) before time t.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Argued, not tested: the authors say immigrants typically cannot predict either the time of treatment or the specific programme to which they may be assigned. Given this assumption, no exclusion restrictions are needed.

implies_edges.from: Entry into an active labour-market programme at time t
implies_edges.to: Hazard rate to regular employment before time t

key_assumptions.assumption: Mixed proportional hazard (MPH) specification of both the employment hazard and the programme-entry hazards, with piecewise constant baseline hazards.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as the modelling assumption under which the treatment effects are non-parametrically identified; not tested.

formal.as_written: θu(tu|x(tu), d1(tu), d2(tu), νu) = λu(tu) exp(x(tu)βu + d1(tu)δ1 + d2(tu)δ2 + νu)

key_assumptions.assumption: Selection into programmes on unobservables is captured by time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity terms that are allowed to be correlated across the employment hazard and the programme hazards.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Built into the likelihood: the correlation between the unobserved term in the employment hazard and those in the programme hazards is unrestricted; no separate test is reported.

key_assumptions.assumption: The joint distribution of the unobserved heterogeneity terms is discrete with 2 x 2 mass points (Heckman and Singer), so the unobserved components of selection into the J programmes are perfectly correlated.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as a simplification; the paper notes that the number of mass points found in applications of this method is typically low.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimated effects are effects of the first ALMP spell: spells of persons participating more than once are right censored at the duration where the second programme period begins.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated in the data section; about 20% of ALMP participants participate more than once.

threats_discussed: Non-random selection into labour-market programmes on observed and unobserved covariates
Endogeneity of the decision to participate in language training and of progression in language proficiency (selection into language courses is not modelled)
No information on proficiency in Danish for immigrants who have not participated in language courses (31% of all immigrants, 24% of those initially receiving social assistance)
Short observation period, so the estimates are short-run estimates in which the negative lock-in effects are relatively important
robustness_checks: Three model specifications (Model 1: ALMPs pooled; Model 2: six programme types; Model 3: adds language-course track placement and lock-in interaction effects), each estimated on two samples
Alternative categorisations of 'age' and 'number of visits to the doctor' did not change the main results
Post-programme interaction effects for simultaneous participation in language courses and ALMPs were estimated and were clearly insignificant
unresolved_confounders: No information on labour-market experience in the country of origin
No information on educational level, except that track placement for language-course participants indicates whether the person is illiterate or has a low or high level of schooling
No information on proficiency in Danish for immigrants who have not participated in language courses

estimator.value: Maximum likelihood estimation of a bivariate timing-of-events duration model (Abbring and van den Berg, 2003): mixed proportional hazard rates for the duration to regular employment and for the duration to programme entry, with piecewise constant baseline hazards and a discrete (Heckman-Singer) 2 x 2 mass-point distribution of the unobserved heterogeneity terms.

key_assumptions.assumption: Mixed proportional hazard (MPH) specification of both the employment hazard and the programme-entry hazards, with piecewise constant baseline hazards.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as the modelling assumption under which the treatment effects are non-parametrically identified; not tested.

key_assumptions.assumption: Selection into programmes on unobservables is captured by time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity terms that are allowed to be correlated across the employment hazard and the programme hazards.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Built into the likelihood: the correlation between the unobserved term in the employment hazard and those in the programme hazards is unrestricted; no separate test is reported.

key_assumptions.assumption: The joint distribution of the unobserved heterogeneity terms is discrete with 2 x 2 mass points (Heckman and Singer), so the unobserved components of selection into the J programmes are perfectly correlated.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as a simplification; the paper notes that the number of mass points found in applications of this method is typically low.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimated effects are effects of the first ALMP spell: spells of persons participating more than once are right censored at the duration where the second programme period begins.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated in the data section; about 20% of ALMP participants participate more than once.

threats_discussed: Non-random selection into labour-market programmes on observed and unobserved covariates
Endogeneity of the decision to participate in language training and of progression in language proficiency (selection into language courses is not modelled)
No information on proficiency in Danish for immigrants who have not participated in language courses (31% of all immigrants, 24% of those initially receiving social assistance)
Short observation period, so the estimates are short-run estimates in which the negative lock-in effects are relatively important
robustness_checks: Three model specifications (Model 1: ALMPs pooled; Model 2: six programme types; Model 3: adds language-course track placement and lock-in interaction effects), each estimated on two samples
Alternative categorisations of 'age' and 'number of visits to the doctor' did not change the main results
Post-programme interaction effects for simultaneous participation in language courses and ALMPs were estimated and were clearly insignificant
unresolved_confounders: No information on labour-market experience in the country of origin
No information on educational level, except that track placement for language-course participants indicates whether the person is illiterate or has a low or high level of schooling
No information on proficiency in Danish for immigrants who have not participated in language courses

definition.value: Model 3 interaction between the time-varying indicator for currently participating in mixed special programmes, designed to improve personal and vocational skills through combinations of different measures and the time-varying indicator for currently participating in Danish language courses; it measures the additional lock-in effect of simultaneous participation.

definition.value: The exit rate from the date of residence permit into regular employment, modelled as a mixed proportional hazard (equation (4)) on weekly event histories; the reported coefficient is the change in the logarithm of this hazard rate per one-unit change in the variable.

timing.value: Weekly event history beginning at the date of residence permit and ending in the last week of the sample period (or at emigration or death); durations are measured in weeks and the baseline hazard is piecewise constant over quarters.

units.value: change in the logarithm of the hazard rate to regular employment when the variable is changed by one unit, holding all other variables constant (log hazard ratio)

magnitude.interpretation: All these interaction effects are negative as expected, and they are statistically significant for three or four of the six programmes (depending on the estimation sample).

definition.value: A time-varying variable for progression in language proficiency measured in deviations from the initial level; progression is observed when an immigrant begins taking courses at a higher level or sublevel (completion of courses is not observed). The sum of initial proficiency and progression gives current proficiency in Danish.

timing.value: Time-varying, measured week by week since the date of residence permit.

definition.value: The exit rate from the date of residence permit into regular employment, modelled as a mixed proportional hazard (equation (4)) on weekly event histories; the reported coefficient is the change in the logarithm of this hazard rate per one-unit change in the variable.

timing.value: Weekly event history beginning at the date of residence permit and ending in the last week of the sample period (or at emigration or death); durations are measured in weeks and the baseline hazard is piecewise constant over quarters.

units.value: change in the logarithm of the hazard rate to regular employment when the variable is changed by one unit, holding all other variables constant (log hazard ratio)

magnitude.interpretation: Both initial proficiency and progression in proficiency have highly significant positive effects in all models.

estimand.target_population: Newly arrived immigrants in Denmark covered by the municipal integration programme: immigrants who (1) received their residence permit in 2000-2002, (2) were 16-64 years of age at the time of arrival, (3) are from non-EU and non-Nordic countries, (4) are refugees or family reunified.
estimand.time_horizon: Time-varying over the spell from residence permit to employment

population.description: All immigrants who (1) received their residence permit in 2000-2002, (2) were 16-64 years of age at the time of arrival, (3) are from non-EU and non-Nordic countries, (4) are refugees or family reunified (21,568 immigrants).
population.ages: 16-64 years of age at the time of arrival / at receipt of the residence permit
population.period: Residence permits granted in 2000-2002; event histories followed from the date of residence permit
subgroups_defined: All immigrants meeting the four criteria
Immigrants who received social assistance from the time of residence permit
Language-course participants, by track (1, 2, 3)
Participants in each of the six types of active labour-market programme
population.selection: Administrative universe of immigrants in Denmark, restricted to those receiving a residence permit in 2000-2002 (ALMP participation data are not available before 2000; 2002 is the last observation year), aged 16-64 at arrival, from non-EU and non-Nordic countries, and refugees or family reunified.

identification.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used for the language-course variables: selection into language courses is not modelled, the variables enter the employment hazard as time-varying regressors alongside a rich set of observed controls and time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity, and the authors state that these effects may not be interpreted as causal.

key_assumptions.assumption: Selection into language courses is not modelled; participation in language training and progression in language proficiency may be endogenous, and the authors state that these effects may not be interpreted as causal.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Conceded, not addressed: the paper argues only that track assignment is largely determined by predetermined educational level, and states explicitly that the language effects do not have a causal interpretation.

key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as the modelling framework; not tested.

formal.as_written: θu(tu|x(tu), d1(tu), d2(tu), νu) = λu(tu) exp(x(tu)βu + d1(tu)δ1 + d2(tu)δ2 + νu)

key_assumptions.assumption: Time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity in the employment hazard, with a discrete 2 x 2 mass-point distribution, absorbs permanent unobserved differences between immigrants.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Built into the likelihood; no separate test is reported.

key_assumptions.assumption: Language skills are unobserved for immigrants who do not participate in language courses; for them the initial-proficiency and progression variables are set to zero.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as an important limitation: non-participants may have varying levels of proficiency and different changes in proficiency with exposure to the Danish language.

threats_discussed: Non-random selection into labour-market programmes on observed and unobserved covariates
Endogeneity of the decision to participate in language training and of progression in language proficiency (selection into language courses is not modelled)
No information on proficiency in Danish for immigrants who have not participated in language courses (31% of all immigrants, 24% of those initially receiving social assistance)
Short observation period, so the estimates are short-run estimates in which the negative lock-in effects are relatively important
robustness_checks: Three model specifications (Model 1: ALMPs pooled; Model 2: six programme types; Model 3: adds language-course track placement and lock-in interaction effects), each estimated on two samples
Alternative categorisations of 'age' and 'number of visits to the doctor' did not change the main results
Post-programme interaction effects for simultaneous participation in language courses and ALMPs were estimated and were clearly insignificant
unresolved_confounders: No information on labour-market experience in the country of origin
No information on educational level, except that track placement for language-course participants indicates whether the person is illiterate or has a low or high level of schooling
No information on proficiency in Danish for immigrants who have not participated in language courses
